ai.description: Murray's Frog (Dicroglossidae) reaches 6–8 cm. It is olive-brown with dark spots and a distinctive yellow or white mid-ventral sternal patch. The skin is granular with prominent dorsolateral folds.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Chrysopaa sternosignata* is best distinguished by the prominent, dark, V-shaped or heart-shaped glandular patch located on its chest, which is absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: Murray's Frog inhabits high-altitude streams and rocky pools in the Himalayas and Hindu Kush, typically found between 1,500 and 3,500 meters in alpine or forest zones.
ai.behavior: Murray’s Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining submerged in cold mountain streams during the day and emerging at night to forage along the rocky banks.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Chrysopaa sternosignata* is an oviparous breeder that lays eggs in mountain streams. Breeding occurs from May to August, with females depositing large, submerged clutches.
ai.distributionRemarks: Chrysopaa sternosignata is endemic to the high-altitude regions of the Himalayas, primarily occurring in Kashmir and Ladakh at elevations between 2,000 and 4,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Chrysopaa sternosignata* is a series of short, high-pitched, metallic chirps emitted from rocky mountain streams.
